subject: The miniaturized House T'sarran spy
fact: The spy is a tiny, sentient operative of House T'sarran, capable of independent thought and violent resistance, contained in a bag alongside Glabbagool, and has been carried by the party for days without formal acknowledgment.
source_quote: the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him... we'd had to open it to show the guards Glabbagool, and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him

subject: The Note: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.'
fact: A handwritten note found on Khell-Vire’s desk, unattributed and unrecognized by either him or Zalthir. It links Zalthir’s journey through the Underdark to a prophetic event — the singing of the Bone King — suggesting a hidden timeline, a ritual countdown, or a spiritual threshold that has already begun to activate through the degraded chant and the spy’s infection.

subject: the shadow step and hit combination
fact: The shadow step and hit combination is Zalthir’s self-developed technique that defies the manual, redeems his lack of skill, and is recognized by Khell-Vire as the most interesting thing about him.
source_quote: It is your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills in all other possible areas.

subject: the shadow tentacles
fact: The shadow tentacles are the eldritch tattoo Zalthir grew as part of his self-built combat style, rejected by the manual but validated by Khell-Vire.
source_quote: I mean, I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.

subject: the sunblade
fact: The sunblade, Dawnbringer, is a late Netherese-era weapon that sustained three to four thousand years of darkness exposure and requires light and mourning to heal.
source_quote: Late Netherese-era recovery, sun-worship origin, sustained darkness exposure of approximately three to four thousand years.

subject: the vial of Resonant Slime
fact: The vial of Resonant Slime is the artifact produced by the sage of xenobiology after being convinced of the gelatinous cube’s sentience, and which Glabbagool was very pleased to receive.
source_quote: The sage... produced a vial of Resonant Slime. Glabbagool was very pleased.

subject: the whisper of the ledger
fact: The whisper of the ledger is the unconscious mental audit Daz runs — tracking debts, knowledge, and losses — a learned grammar of Menzoberranzan he cannot yet name.
source_quote: I have been running that audit unconsciously since before I could name it.

subject: thorin's pocket drow
fact: Thorin refers to a drow as 'Pocket Drow' in the context of a sentient gelatinous cube's companion.
source_quote: Pocket Drow

subject: wall memory
fact: The south wall of the inn remembers where the wizard fell; it is not painted over.
source_quote: That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: zalthir's shadow technique
fact: Zalthir chose option C of the three specialized shadow techniques offered by Khell-Vire.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C

subject: Bahamut's Contingency
fact: The possibility of Bahamut having a contingency plan for the phenomenon of demon lords rewriting the language of wells and shapes is filed as an open question, unresolved and unverified.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have had a contingency plan for this. I filed it under open questions and kept writing.

subject: connection between Elin and Daz
fact: Grygum suspects a tenuous connection between Elin’s condition and Daz’s head pressure, suggesting a shared origin.
source_quote: There's some kind of tenuous connection there?

subject: Dawnbringer’s first wielder
fact: The identity and fate of Dawnbringer’s original wielder — the corpse she was found in — remains unspoken and unprocessed, a silent wound that surfaces only in moments of profound stillness.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet.

subject: Daz'issin
fact: Daz suspects that Daz'issin — the softened name meaning 'small shadow' — may be his true name, tied to a lost maternal lineage.
source_quote: I asked if she knew my name. She did. I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.

subject: Daz's Identity as the Survivor
fact: Daz suspects he is the sole surviving child of the house struck from the fourth seat — the 'blithering idiot' who escaped annihilation. His amnesia, headache, and innate understanding of Menzoberranzan's structures align with this possibility, but no confirmation exists in the public record.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: Daz's mental deterioration
fact: Daz's unexplained silence and temple-touching during the journey to Candlekeep may indicate the spreading madness from the Underdark has followed him to the surface, and its origin and resolution remain unanswered.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me... His hand went to his temple and stayed there... I noticed. I didn't say anything yet.

subject: Daz's patron
fact: Daz seeks to learn who his patron is, as it may be connected to his name and the act of striking.
source_quote: "I do want to know who protected me, that would be useful, yeah."

subject: Daz's patron
fact: Yvenne redirected inquiry from Daz's name to his patron, implying the identity of his protector may be more significant — or more dangerous — than his own origin.

subject: Daz’s true identity
fact: Daz’s lack of memory and his possible connection to a wiped-out noble house — specifically the 'blithering idiot' survivor — remains an unresolved thread, with Sister Yvenne deliberately withholding confirmation to observe his reaction.
source_quote: Unclear.

subject: Daz's true lineage
fact: The suppression of Daz'issin's record and Yvenne's evasive behavior suggest Daz's origin is tied to a destroyed house whose existence contradicts the official record, and whose survival may still be possible.

subject: Daz's true name
fact: Daz wonders if his name 'Daz' is a shortened form of 'Daz'issin', a name used by his mother.
source_quote: I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.

subject: Daz's true origin
fact: Daz may be the last living bearer of the name Daz'issin — a name tied to extinct houses and erased records — and his survival may be linked to a protected lineage that was deliberately hidden, making his identity a living anomaly in Menzoberranzan’s official history.
source_quote: I asked if she knew my name. She did. I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.

subject: hearing voices from below
fact: Multiple individuals — Elin, Daz, and others — are experiencing auditory distortions that are not magical but stem from a structural corruption bleeding up from the Underdark, suggesting that the demon lords’ influence is no longer confined to the deep places but is rewriting how the surface perceives reality.
source_quote: Something from below was bleeding up, that it was affecting how people processed what reached them.

subject: Identity of Dawnbringer’s Previous Wielder
fact: The identity and fate of Dawnbringer’s previous wielder remain unknown, but their death in proximity to the blade triggered her trauma, and the silence that followed the question suggests unresolved guilt, betrayal, or loss tied to their final moments.
source_quote: He asked about the previous wielder. The corpse she had been found in, he said. Whether that person had been — had been her wielder.

subject: identity of the monument's commissioner
fact: The origin of the monument’s design — particularly the inclusion of the Stroudite inscription — remains unexplained, with the Metalworkers Guild’s possible Stroudite members and the priest’s admission that it was 'a gift' leaving the true motive ambiguous.
source_quote: It was a gift... we decided the inscription could remain.

subject: Manual vs. Innovation
fact: A recurring narrative thread: Zalthir consistently ignores official manuals, builds superior techniques through intuition and combat experience, and is later told by authorities that his innovations are the most valuable thing about him — suggesting the manuals are fundamentally flawed about him.
source_quote: The manual was still wrong about him. But what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his.

subject: missing appendix
fact: The missing appendix in *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe* was removed by a razor, indicating intentional erasure.
source_quote: The appendix was missing. I looked at the cut. It was mechanical. A razor. Not age, not water damage, not the slow forgetting of paper that has been handled too many times. A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: sealed house record
fact: A house record in Menzoberranzan has been sealed by the public record keeper, implying a powerful entity intervened.
source_quote: Then she told me there was one house she could not speak of in the room. Not because she would not — because the public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.

subject: Sentience Beyond Biology
fact: A philosophical thread challenging the assumption that sentience requires a brain — demonstrated by the gelatinous cube learning monk ways, the blade Dawnbringer developing a personality, and the monk Khell-Vire recognizing hidden depth in unorthodox expressions of power.
source_quote: Can a mindless digestive system achieve—

subject: Shadow Monk Rediscovery
fact: Zalthir’s unorthodox technique may not be a personal innovation, but the reawakening of a lost shadow monk tradition — one that valued combination over perfection — now being recognized by Khell-Vire as the true path.
source_quote: It is your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills.

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: A Dwarven inscription referencing Stroud — 'The move is yours' — appears on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin, creating unspoken tension between factions, with no one certain whether it was an oversight, a gift, or a quiet act of defiance.
source_quote: The inscription shares language with Stroud... Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin... they had either not noticed or not cared enough to remove it.

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: A Stroudite inscription appears on a monument dedicated to a Bahamutian paladin, despite religious differences.
source_quote: Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin in a town I'd barely heard of, and whoever commissioned it had either not noticed or not cared enough to remove it.

subject: The 'blithering idiot' survivor
fact: The identity of the sole survivor of a destroyed noble house — described dismissively as a 'blithering idiot' — may be Daz himself, suggesting he is not merely an amnesiac but the living remnant of a forbidden lineage.
source_quote: Unclear.

subject: the Bone King sings
fact: The phrase "the Bone King sings" appears on a note in Khell-Vire's office and is unknown to Zalthir and Khell-Vire.
source_quote: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.*

subject: The Bone King's Song
fact: The phrase 'until the Bone King sings' appears in an unexplained note and resonates with the degraded chant, the spy’s behavior, and the madness spreading from the Underdark. It is not a myth — it is a countdown. The question is not whether it will happen, but what happens when it does — and whether Zalthir, the spy, Glabbagool, and the scholar are all instruments of its arrival.

subject: The Bone King's Song
fact: The phrase 'until the Bone King sings' is an unresolved, possibly prophetic anchor tied to Zalthir’s journey and the Shadow Monk Lineage’s hidden history, with no known origin or meaning in Candlekeep’s records.
source_quote: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.*

subject: The Chant Contagion
fact: A precise, replicating corruption in a sacred chant has appeared in four unrelated individuals: the spy, Eldred, the Field Ward Preacher, and the young scholar. It is not random madness but a patterned degradation — a ritual infection, a linguistic virus, or a hidden doctrine being transmitted. Whoever created it is still active. Whoever understands it can stop it — or unleash it.

subject: the chant pattern
fact: The degraded chant pattern matches those seen in Eldred and the Field Ward Preacher, both of whom experienced madness.
source_quote: I have seen it before. Twice. Eldred had it, earlier in the journey — the man who went insane. The Field Ward Preacher had it too.

subject: The Degraded Chant
fact: A specific, non-beginner-level degradation in the cadence of a liturgical chant — involving false syncopation and breath timing — has been observed in three individuals, two of whom later went insane. The pattern may indicate a corrupted doctrine, a cursed practice, or a deliberate mimicry of sacred ritual.
source_quote: The same pattern. The same wrongness by a hair. ... I wrote it down. The exact cadence, the placement of the false syncopation, the point in the verse where the chant bent away from the original.

subject: The Kenku's Restraint
fact: The bard's song references Whistler, a kenku thief of an earlier age who, presented with Tiamat's complete hoard, took only what was necessary for legitimate expenses — a pattern of disciplined restraint that contrasts with typical human greed or panic.
source_quote: Whistler had apparently made a line-item budget. ... Most people, faced with the complete hoard of Tiamat, would either take everything or panic and take nothing.

subject: the move is yours
fact: The Stroudite inscription 'The move is yours' on Tarvis Ulain’s monument is an unresolved puzzle linking Daggerford to Waterdeep’s Castle Ward statue and the legacy of Stroud — suggesting a hidden network of influence, possibly tied to the demon lords’ spreading corruption, and inviting interpretation from those who understand the game.
source_quote: The move is yours. ... Same line as the Castle Ward statue in Waterdeep. The one connected to Stroud.

subject: the nature of the monk’s path
fact: Glabbagool’s question — whether watching the spy makes him more or less of a monk — and Zalthir’s affirmation of it, suggest that the path of the monk may lie not in isolation, but in the acceptance of chaotic, unchosen responsibility.
source_quote: 'Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?' 'Absolutely,' I said.

subject: The nature of Zalthir’s shadow technique
fact: Zalthir’s hybrid method — combining shadow step and precise strikes — is not documented in any known shadow monk texts, suggesting it may be a rediscovery of a lost tradition or an entirely new evolution — one that may redefine the path of shadow monks.
source_quote: There is something special about how you hit.

subject: The Sealed House
fact: One house cannot be spoken of in the room because its record is sealed — not by secrecy, but because the librarian *is* the public record. Accessing its truth requires bypassing the library’s own architecture, implying the suppression is institutional, not accidental.
source_quote: There was one house she could not speak of in the room. Not because she would not — because the public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.

subject: The six-pointed star drawings
fact: Elin draws the same six-pointed star on every flat surface as an act of insistence, not madness.
source_quote: She draws the same shape on every flat surface.

subject: the spread of madness
fact: The madness observed in the Underdark has continued to affect Daz after reaching the surface.
source_quote: Whatever was happening to Daz had started below ground and apparently had not stopped at the surface.

subject: the spy's fate
fact: The spy’s future is uncertain: Candlekeep will release her eventually with a warning, but she refuses to accept this, and her actions after release may provoke House T'sarran or destabilize the region.
source_quote: Eventually, we will release her at our gate with a warning... She did not take this well. She had opinions. Several of them.

subject: The Spy’s True Desire
fact: The spy demanded imprisonment, not freedom. This contradicts her nature as a House T'sarran operative. Why? Is she trying to contain the chant within her? Is she afraid of what she will become if released? Or has she already become something else — something that cannot be controlled by her masters?

subject: The Stroudite inscription on Tarvis’s monument
fact: Someone placed a Stroudite inscription on a Bahamutian paladin’s monument, and no one removed it because it was a gift.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild... we decided the inscription could remain. After all — wasn't Tarvis trying to save us all, regardless of what actually happened in that game of chess?

subject: The Struck Fourth Seat
fact: The fourth seat was 'struck' — not eliminated — suggesting the house or its record was altered but not fully erased. The act required archive privileges, significant resources, and plausible deniability. The identity of the house, the reason for the strike, and the current status of its survivors remain hidden behind sealed doors.
source_quote: Struck. Didn't mean eliminated. It means they struck it, but maybe they didn't eliminate it, and therefore, like, it didn't happen? Is that why I feel like it's different?

subject: The Underdark Curriculum
fact: Zalthir’s survival in the Underdark represents an alternative, unrecorded curriculum that contradicts Candlekeep’s formal training — a hidden path where practicality overrides doctrine, and where learning is measured by survival, not scrolls.
source_quote: He had survived the Underdark, which is a different curriculum.

subject: The wells are not wells anymore
fact: Elin’s first words after restoration were 'The wells are not wells anymore,' a sentence that means more than it says.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: the wells are not wells anymore
fact: Elin’s utterance — 'The wells are not wells anymore' — is a cryptic revelation that the Underdark’s corruption is transforming fundamental aspects of reality, and that the surface world is losing its ability to interpret basic metaphors — a philosophical thread that connects perception, language, and the unraveling of meaning.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: The wells are not wells anymore
fact: Elin’s utterance — 'The wells are not wells anymore' — is a cryptic, high-stakes thread. It implies a transformation of fundamental metaphysical or spatial structures, possibly referencing corrupted conduits of perception or reality itself, and is not yet interpretable.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: Thorin’s Headache and Candlekeep’s Knowledge
fact: Thorin’s unexplained headache, triggered by proximity to Candlekeep’s accumulated knowledge, hints at a deeper, possibly magical or psychic resonance between his consciousness and the library’s archives — a thread that remains unexplored but is implicitly significant.
source_quote: My head had been complaining since we arrived at Candlekeep. The proximity — to the knowledge, or to whatever sat underneath the knowledge — was producing a friction I had been mis-attributing to the sun all day.

subject: Underdark corruption spreading to the surface
fact: Something from the Underdark is bleeding upward, affecting perception and causing voices and hallucinations on the surface.
source_quote: something from below was bleeding up, ... the madness from the Underdark ... was not, apparently, staying below. It was reaching up.

subject: Zalthir’s Unlearned Mastery
fact: Zalthir’s techniques are wrong by the scrolls — but they work. He did not learn shadow steps; he survived them. His trial revealed that Candlekeep’s system cannot measure him — and perhaps does not want to. Is he the next Shadow Monk? Or the last one who broke the mold? And what happens when the Bone King sings, and the only one who can respond is the one who never learned how to?
